g.text: Global growth reference for infants, children, and adolescents, as defined by the World Health Organization.

text.style: font-size: 7.75px; font-family: 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', sans-serif; fill: #777777

g.text: Note: The curves step down slightly at age 2, where height starts being measured standing up rather than lying down, and at age 5, where WHO’s standards for under-fives

text.style: font-size: 7.75px; font-family: 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', sans-serif; fill: #777777

g.text: give way to its reference for older children. The under-fives standards show how children grow in good conditions; the reference for older children describes how an earlier

text.style: font-size: 7.75px; font-family: 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', sans-serif; fill: #777777

g.text: sample did grow. A child is stunted if they are more than two standard deviations shorter than the median for their age, which is the shaded area’s lower edge: 2.3% of the
